name: Business Domain Profile
description: Validate domain ownership, company identity, and business legitimacy.
checklist: Is there a real company registered to this domain?
Does the organisation name on the domain match the claimed identity in the alert?
When was the domain registered and how old is it?
Does the email format match what Hunter.io reports for this org?
Is there an archived history — or is this a brand new domain?
Does the LinkedIn/Crunchbase profile match the claimed company size and sector?
Is the domain registered in the expected country for the claimed company?
Are there subdomains or related domains that look suspicious (crt.sh)?
What technology stack does the domain run — does it match a legitimate business?
Has the domain been involved in any data leaks or exposed services (LeakIX)?
expectedOutcome: Determine whether the domain is associated with a legitimate, identifiable business or appears to be a newly registered, unregistered, or spoofed entity.

name: IP Triage
description: Investigate an IP address for reputation, geolocation, and threat context.
checklist: Is the IP known internet background noise (scanners, crawlers)?
Is it flagged as malicious by multiple reputation sources?
Is it a VPN, proxy, Tor exit node, or residential proxy?
What ASN and hosting provider owns it?
Is it associated with any known threat actors or malware campaigns?
What ports and services are exposed (Shodan/Censys)?
Was any internal connection to this IP successful?
Is the activity one-directional or bidirectional?
What is the internal context — which assets communicated with it?
Should this IP be blocked, monitored, tuned, or escalated?
expectedOutcome: Determine whether the IP is a known threat, internet noise, or a legitimate service. Decide on block, monitor, tune, or close as benign.

name: Domain Triage
description: Investigate a domain for reputation, registration, and infrastructure context.
checklist: When was the domain registered? Newly registered domains are higher risk.
Does the domain have valid WHOIS data or privacy-shielded registration?
What is the hosting infrastructure (IP, ASN, CDN)?
Is the domain flagged by any reputation sources?
Are there suspicious subdomains in Certificate Transparency logs?
Does it share infrastructure with known malicious domains?
Is there DNS evidence of past use (passive DNS)?
Was the domain resolved internally and was the connection successful?
Is this a typosquat or lookalike of a legitimate domain?
Should this domain be blocked or monitored?
expectedOutcome: Assess domain age, infrastructure, and reputation to determine if it is malicious, suspicious, or benign. Recommend block or tune.

name: URL / Phishing
description: Analyse a URL for phishing indicators, malicious content, and redirect behaviour.
checklist: Does the URL use HTTPS or HTTP? Self-signed certificate?
Does the domain look like a typosquat or impersonation of a legitimate brand?
When was the domain registered?
Does the URL contain encoded or obfuscated content?
Does the URL contain sensitive parameters (tokens, session IDs)?
Are there redirect chains before reaching the final page?
What does the page render show (credential form, fake login, etc.)?
Has the URL been flagged by Google Safe Browsing or other blacklists?
Did internal users click the link? Was the connection successful?
Is this part of a broader phishing campaign?
Should you take down the site and report to hosting provider?
expectedOutcome: Confirm whether the URL is phishing or malicious. Identify impacted users. Submit for takedown if appropriate. Block domain/URL.

name: Spam Source
description: Investigate a suspected spam-sending IP or domain, including email authentication checks.
checklist: Does the sending IP have a poor email reputation (Talos, AbuseIPDB)?
Did SPF pass, fail, or softfail?
Did DKIM validate correctly?
Is DMARC configured and what is the policy?
Is the sending domain newly registered or privacy-shielded?
Is the sender address spoofed or a lookalike?
Were other recipients targeted from the same campaign?
Was the email delivered or quarantined?
Should the sending IP or domain be blocked at the email gateway?
expectedOutcome: Confirm spam origin, assess impact to recipients, and recommend gateway rule or block for sending IP/domain.

name: Malware / Hash
description: Investigate a file hash for known malware, sandboxed behaviour, and threat actor association.
checklist: What is the detection ratio across AV engines?
What malware family is it classified as?
Is it associated with a known threat actor or campaign?
What is the file type and first/last seen date?
Are there sandbox reports showing dynamic behaviour?
What C2 infrastructure does the sample connect to?
Was this file executed on any internal endpoints?
Was it delivered via email, web download, or USB?
Should affected endpoints be isolated and reimaged?
Are there related IOCs to enrich (C2 IPs, dropped files)?
expectedOutcome: Confirm whether the hash is known malware, determine scope of infection, and identify response actions (isolate, reimage, block).

name: Suspicious Connection
description: Investigate a suspicious network connection — IP, domain, or URL — seen in firewall, proxy, or EDR logs.
checklist: Is the destination IP or domain known malicious?
Is it internet background noise (GreyNoise)?
What services are exposed on the destination IP?
Was the connection internal-to-external or vice versa?
Was the connection allowed or blocked?
What internal asset made the connection?
Is this C2 communication, exfiltration, or benign lookup?
Are there other internal hosts making similar connections?
What is the data volume and connection duration?
Should the destination be blocked and the source asset investigated?
expectedOutcome: Determine if the connection represents a threat (C2, exfiltration, exploitation). Identify scope and recommend block or investigation of affected assets.

name: WAF / Web Attack
description: Investigate an IP or domain seen in WAF alerts or web attack logs.
checklist: Is the attacking IP known internet background noise?
Is it a VPN, proxy, Tor exit, or residential proxy?
What WAF rules were triggered and how many times?
Was the attack targeted or part of mass scanning?
Was any request successful (2xx response)?
What attack type was it (SQLi, XSS, path traversal, RCE)?
Is the same IP attacking multiple assets?
Should the IP be blocked at WAF, firewall, or both?
Is there a detection gap — should a new rule be created?
Is this a false positive that needs tuning?

internalSearches.label: WAF logs — allowed requests from IP

expectedOutcome: Determine if the WAF alert is a targeted attack or background noise. Tune detection rules and block persistent attackers.

name: Dark Web / Credential Exposure
description: Check if an email, domain, or IP has appeared in dark web leak sites, breach data, or stealer logs.
checklist: Has the email address or domain appeared in known breach databases?
Are there stealer log entries with credentials for this domain?
Has the organisation appeared on ransomware group leak sites?
What data types were exposed (credentials, PII, financial)?
Which accounts are affected?
When was the data exposed?
Have the exposed credentials been rotated?
Has the incident been reported to affected users?
Is there ongoing dark web activity suggesting active targeting?
expectedOutcome: Identify exposed credentials or sensitive data, notify affected users, force password resets, and assess breach impact.

name: Takedown Reporting
description: Gather evidence and submit takedown requests for phishing or malicious domains/URLs.
checklist: Have you captured screenshot evidence of the malicious page?
Have you recorded the full URL, hosting IP, and registrar?
Have you submitted to Google Safe Browsing?
Have you submitted to phish.report for automated takedown?
Have you reported to the hosting provider abuse contact?
Have you reported to the domain registrar?
Have you reported to NCSC or relevant national authority if applicable?
Have you blocked the domain internally while takedown is in progress?
Have you documented the evidence trail for the case record?

internalSearches.label: Email gateway — URLs delivered from this domain
Proxy — users who accessed the domain

expectedOutcome: Submit takedown requests to relevant parties, document evidence, block internally, and confirm site goes offline.

name: Ransomware Context
description: Investigate IOCs associated with a suspected ransomware incident.
checklist: Has the organisation appeared on ransomware leak sites?
Is the hash a known ransomware binary?
What ransomware family is associated with the IOC?
What are the known C2 IPs and domains for this family?
What TTPs does this ransomware use (MITRE ATT&CK)?
Are internal assets communicating with known C2 infrastructure?
Has encryption started? Which assets are affected?
Have backups been checked and isolated?
Has the incident response team been notified?
Has legal and management been briefed?

internalSearches.label: Backup systems — last good backup check

expectedOutcome: Identify the ransomware family, assess scope, contain affected systems, initiate IR plan, and preserve evidence for forensics.

name: External Exposure
description: Assess the external attack surface of an IP, domain, or CIDR range.
checklist: What ports and services are publicly exposed?
Are there exposed admin interfaces (RDP, SSH, VNC, web admin panels)?
Are SSL certificates valid and not expired?
Are there unexpected subdomains in Certificate Transparency logs?
Is there sensitive content exposed (login pages, default credentials)?
Are there known CVEs associated with the exposed services?
What cloud/hosting provider is the asset on?
Is the asset in scope for your organisation?
Should any exposed services be restricted or patched?

internalSearches.label: Firewall — inbound allowed rules for IP

expectedOutcome: Map external attack surface, identify unintended exposure, and recommend remediation (close ports, apply patches, restrict access).

name: CVE Context
description: Look up a CVE ID for CISA KEV exploitation status, severity, and affected products.
checklist: Is this CVE in the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue?
What is the CVSS base score and vector?
What products and versions are affected?
Is there public exploit code available (ExploitDB, GitHub)?
Is there evidence of active in-the-wild exploitation?
Are internal assets running the affected product and version?
Has the vendor issued a patch or mitigation?
What is the remediation due date if in CISA KEV?
Has the patch been applied or a compensating control implemented?
Is there a detection rule or sigma rule available for this CVE?
expectedOutcome: Confirm whether the CVE is actively exploited and if internal assets are affected. Prioritise patching based on CISA KEV status and CVSS score.

name: Email Header Review
description: Analyse email headers for routing anomalies, authentication failures, and spoofing indicators.
checklist: Did SPF pass, fail, or softfail for the sending IP?
Did DKIM verify correctly?
What is the DMARC policy and did the message pass?
Does the From address match the sending domain?
Are there unusual relay hops or unexpected sending IPs?
Is the sending IP on any email blacklists?
Does the email contain URLs? Have they been analysed?
Does the email contain attachments? Have they been sandboxed?
Was the email delivered or quarantined by the email gateway?
Does the email impersonate a trusted brand or internal sender?
expectedOutcome: Determine email authenticity, identify spoofing or phishing indicators, assess delivery impact, and recommend gateway block or tune.
